questions.q: When is reporting-only consolidation an appropriate method?
options: When entities have completely different charts of accounts and calendars
When the subsidiary and corporate ledger already share the same chart of accounts and calendar
Only when no intercompany transactions exist
Only for ledgers in the same currency
questions.explain: Reporting-only consolidation is used when structures already align, requiring far less mapping work than balance transfer.

questions.q: What does balance transfer consolidation require that reporting-only consolidation does not?
options: Mapping the subsidiary's chart of accounts to the corporate chart of accounts before importing and posting the mapped balances
Deleting the subsidiary's original ledger
Converting all currencies to EUR specifically
Running revaluation twice per period
questions.explain: Balance transfer consolidation is used when structures differ, which requires chart of accounts mapping before transferring balances into the consolidation ledger.

questions.q: Why can't consolidated entity balances simply be added together once they're in the consolidation ledger?
options: Because addition is not supported in Oracle Fusion
Because intercompany transactions between entities in the group would be double-counted unless eliminated
Because currencies cannot be combined under any circumstances
Because only one entity's balances are ever included
questions.explain: Transactions between group entities (debt, revenue/expense, stock ownership) represent the group dealing with itself and must be eliminated, not simply summed.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the three basic types of elimination entries described in this lesson?
options: Elimination of foreign currency journals
Elimination of intercompany debt
Elimination of the chart of accounts
Elimination of journal approval history
questions.explain: The three basic elimination types are intercompany stock ownership, intercompany debt, and intercompany revenue and expense.

questions.q: Why must the $4,000 IT allocation from LTV Manufacturing Corporation's US entity to its UK entity be eliminated at consolidation?
options: Because it was recorded incorrectly in both entities
Because although it is real to each entity individually, from the group's perspective it is money moving within the same organization, not a transaction with an outside party
Because intercompany transactions are illegal under Oracle Fusion rules
Because only revenue, never expense, needs elimination
questions.explain: From the consolidated group's perspective, an intercompany allocation isn't a transaction with an outside party, so it must be eliminated to avoid overstating consolidated results.
